question: According to reports1, on 24 August 2026 Libya issued a Note Verbale contesting the planned hydrocarbon exploration south of Crete, citing unilateral maritime claims linked to the illegal Turkish-Libyan memorandum of understanding. Libya also threatens Greece with the possible suspension of bilateral delineation negotiations.

The European Council has repeatedly stated that the illegal Turkish-Libyan memorandum violates the sovereign rights of third states, contravenes the Law of the Sea and does not produce legal effects for third states. The continued challenging of Greek sovereign rights calls the practical implementation of European foreign policy into question.
In view of the above, can the Vice-President of the Commission / High Representative of the Union for Foreign Affairs and Security Policy answer the following: 1.

Does she intend to recommend that the Council consider targeted sanctions against natural or legal persons responsible for actions challenging Greek sovereign rights, including the establishment of an appropriate legal framework for restrictive measures?

Does she intend to raise the issue in the Foreign Affairs Council and what specific diplomatic initiatives will she take to implement the conclusions of the European Council and protect the sovereign rights of the Member States?
